signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Yield Disadvantage
signals.text: CHF/JPY downside pressure intensifies as JPY leads G10 performance (+1.218%) while CHF lags (-0.687%), creating a significant 1.904% bilateral spread. JPY's outperformance is supported by a positive ESI (+17.8) and sustained bull-steepening in the US yield curve, which historically favors JPY as a funding currency unwind destination. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) remains the catalyst for resolving the yield gap against the current JPY momentum.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +37.9k (72.1% long) creates significant downside risk if the pair fails to hold above the SMA200 at 0.6925 following China's cooling July CPI data. While AUD benefits from a -70bp OIS carry advantage over the USD, a negative ESI (-11.1) suggests domestic data is underperforming expectations. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 11 Aug is the catalyst for confirming if the current hold bias can withstand softening Chinese demand.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Put Skew + Squeeze Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 157.82 with a JPY COT short of -63.6k reinforcing a potential short-squeeze risk as the pair trades below its SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200. Options markets show a strong put skew (RR -2.20), indicating elevated hedging demand for JPY strength despite the +267bp OIS carry advantage favoring the USD. The BoJ Summary of Opinions on Monday is the catalyst for gauging the sustainability of JPY's recent recovery.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short Short-Squeeze
signals.text: EUR/USD upside momentum toward 1.1633 (SMA200) is supported by a crowded EUR COT short position of -73.0k (only 34% long). The market is pricing a restrictive ECB (real rate +0.13%) against a softening US labor outlook following the weak NFP report, though the +146bp OIS carry advantage still favors the USD. The next ECB meeting (mkt: 53% hike priced) on 10 Sep is the catalyst for confirming the hike bias that supports recent Euro gains.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence Setup
signals.text: NZD/USD shows a divergence between the extreme NZD COT net short of -30.7k (9.7% long) and a leading G10 ESI of +24.4. This creates significant short-squeeze potential toward the 0.6000 level as sustained data beats conflict with pessimistic speculator positioning. The RBNZ hike bias and accommodative real rate of -1.56% will be tested at the next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 100% hike priced) on 2 Sep.
